query:
UPDATE news 
SET blocks = JSON_ARRAY(
  JSON_OBJECT('type', 'text', 'content', 'Scenic designer Brandon PT Davis returns to the New Swan Shakespeare Festival for the 2026 season, bringing his narrative-driven design approach to a repertory lineup that spans two distinct American eras. After previous collaborations with the festival, Davis will create the scenic environment for both The Merry Wives of Windsor Cove—a musical reimagining set in a rock-and-roll 1950s Southern California surf town—and a stark, Dust Bowl–era staging of Romeo and Juliet.'),
  JSON_OBJECT('type', 'header', 'level', 2, 'content', 'The Productions'),
  JSON_OBJECT('type', 'text', 'content', 'Running July 7 through August 30, the season challenges Davis to design a single architectural gesture capable of transforming from a sun-drenched beach party into a landscape of scarcity and survival. Merry Wives will embrace the color and energy of mid-century surf culture, complete with live music and period details that evoke the golden age of California beach life. In contrast, Romeo and Juliet strips the stage back to reflect the harsh realities of the Great Depression, grounding Shakespeare's tragedy in the economic devastation and social upheaval of 1930s America.'),
  JSON_OBJECT('type', 'header', 'level', 2, 'content', 'Design Approach'),
  JSON_OBJECT('type', 'text', 'content', 'The design must support the distinct directorial visions of Eli Simon and Rachael VanWormer while maintaining the flexibility required for true repertory theatre. Davis's approach centers on creating a transformative scenic architecture—one that can shift between eras through lighting, texture, and strategic scenic elements rather than relying on heavy set changes. This challenge is amplified by the intimacy of New Swan's 130-seat mini-Elizabethan theatre, where every design choice is visible and every detail matters.'),
  JSON_OBJECT('type', 'header', 'level', 2, 'content', 'Festival Context'),
  JSON_OBJECT('type', 'text', 'content', 'The New Swan Shakespeare Festival at UC Irvine has built a reputation for bold, innovative productions in its intimate outdoor venue. The mini-Elizabethan theatre creates a unique relationship between performers and audience, demanding scenic design that enhances rather than overwhelms the space. Davis's previous work with the festival demonstrated his ability to craft environments that serve the story while respecting the architectural constraints and opportunities of the venue.'),
  JSON_OBJECT('type', 'header', 'level', 2, 'content', 'Tickets and Season Information'),
  JSON_OBJECT('type', 'text', 'content', 'Tickets for the 2026 season go on sale in April, with performances running through late August. Davis's transformative scenery will provide the visual foundation for a summer of comedy, tragedy, and live music under the stars, demonstrating how a single design can serve radically different theatrical worlds.')
)
WHERE slug = 'returning-to-new-swan-theatre-festival-2026';
